validity.researcher_notes: No gem.wiki page was harvested for P5935 (absent from wiki_citations.json), so this pass went straight to independent primary sources per the source ladder, searching Russian-language terms (Абесса-Кишинев газопровод). EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, real and physical. Moldovatransgaz (mtg.md/ru/news/54) — the Moldovan state gas-transmission operator, i.e. the counterpart TSO on the Moldovan end of this Ukraine-Moldova interconnector — publishes a page listing all 8 trunk gas pipelines it operates in Moldova (656.307 km total), and item 6 is 'Одесса - Кишинев (ОК)' described as a trunk line ('магистраль') supplying gas to consumers of the country, length 44.0 km, diameter 530 mm, capacity 1.3 billion m3/year — an EXACT match to every GEM value on this row (LengthKnown=44.00 km, Diameter=530 mm, Capacity=1.30 bcm/y). A second Moldovatransgaz release (mtg.md/ru/news/77) documents active 2020-2021 reconstruction work (a new 12.85 km section spliced into the existing line, GRS Chisinau-1 briefly taken offline during the tie-in) — direct evidence the asset is alive, maintained, and in current service, not a phantom/GEM-only entity. A third source, Moldovagaz JSC (the parent holding company, a separate corporate page — moldovagaz.md), independently corroborates construction: its GRS-1 Chisinau station history notes the 'Odessa-Chisinau' trunk line (Ду 530, 44 km) was commissioned in 1966, the same year as the GRS-1 station it feeds. CLASSIFICATION: correct. All sources call it a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline) built to supply end consumers, not a gathering/feeder/process line — PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas both stand. DUPLICATE: checked against the 9-PID Ukraine gas roster (P1480, P2387, P3063, P3381/P3382, P3484/P5938, P5989) — none touch Odesa or Chisinau; no name/geography overlap, no double-count risk. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Moldovatransgaz 100% is directly confirmed — Moldovatransgaz's own page names this exact pipeline as one of the 8 it operates ('обслуживает'); StartLocation=Odesa/Ukraine and EndLocation=Chisinau/Moldova match the pipeline's own name and both sources' descriptions. Caveat: Moldovatransgaz's language is 'services/operates' rather than an explicit ownership/title statement, and legal title could formally sit with parent Moldovagaz — treat Owner tier as medium, not high, on that technicality.

validity.recommendation: Do not change GEM's Capacity value (1.30 bcm/y already matches the operator's current published figure) but flag the historical figure for awareness in ResearcherNotes: verify whether the line was ever formally uprated from its original 1966 design capacity, or whether one of the two company sources is simply carrying a stale/incorrect number.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC discrepancy on Capacity, >2x, between two sources from the same Moldovan state-gas corporate group. Moldovatransgaz's current network-overview page (mtg.md/ru/news/54) states the Odesa-Chisinau line's capacity as 1.3 billion m3/year — matching GEM exactly. But Moldovagaz's (the parent JSC) own GRS-1 Chisinau history article (moldovagaz.md) states the pipeline's ORIGINAL 1966 design throughput ('проектная производительность') as 570.0 million normal m3/year (=0.57 bcm/y) — less than half GEM's figure. Both texts otherwise agree exactly on length (44 km) and diameter (530 mm/Ду530), so this isn't a different pipeline being conflated. Two readings are possible: (a) the line was uprated at some point post-1966 from 570 to 1,300 million m3/y (no documentation of such a project found in this pass), or (b) one of the two company sources has carried forward an error. Because GEM's own value matches the CURRENT operator page exactly, I am not proposing a value change — but this is a genuine, material, unresolved disagreement between two sources in the same corporate family, not a clean confirmation, so it is flagged per the material-disagreement rule rather than silently passed.

No dated evidence of any outage/mothballing was found, so 'operating' stands; medium tier because neither source is dated to the present (2026) explicitly, only continuity in the absence of contrary evidence.

Two independent company sources (current operator Moldovatransgaz + parent Moldovagaz's separate historical article) both state 44 km exactly.
Both sources state Ду530 / 530 mm exactly — no unit-conversion round-trip artifact (unlike P1465/P1773 elsewhere in this country's roster).

The pipeline's own name and description tie it to the Odesa junction with Ukraine's gas transmission system, which is the gas-supply origin point feeding into Moldova on this line. Tier medium: this is a reasonable inference from the source's description of the pipeline's Ukrainian-side connection, not a source using the literal field label 'FuelSource'.
The pipeline's name and both sources confirm the Odesa (Ukraine) → Chisinau (Moldova) endpoints.

Moldovatransgaz's own list of the 8 trunk pipelines it operates in Moldova names Odesa-Chisinau explicitly. Ukraine's Gazprom-attribution trap (per country guidance) does not apply here — this line is wholly on the Moldovan side of the border and its operator is unambiguously Moldovan state gas infrastructure, not Gazprom. Held at medium (not high) because the source's language is operational ('обслуживает' / services) rather than an explicit ownership/title statement, and only one source makes the claim.
